title: Big Ladle, Small Ladle
markdown:
The sun peeked. Gold light tickled Leo awake. Soup day! Fern the fawn twitched her nose. The air smelled sweet. She trotted to Aunt Rosa’s cottage.

Leo was there, peeking at the soup pot. "Oh dear," Aunt Rosa said. "The pot is almost empty! We need more broth for friends."

Leo pointed. "A big ladle!" Fern nudged a smaller one. "This one is tiny!"

Aunt Rosa brought three bowls: tiny, medium, big. With the big ladle, Swoosh! The big bowl was full. "Just enough for this one!" she said.

Leo took the small ladle. Plink, plonk. He poured into the tiny bowl. It filled just a little! "Wow!" Leo gasped. "This one holds much less!"

Fern watched. Her eyes sparkled. She took the medium ladle. "The big ladle fills the big bowl fast," she murmured. "The small one fills the small bowl slow."

"Exactly!" Aunt Rosa clapped. "We need lots of soup, super-fast! Let's fill the big pot!"

Leo grinned. He grabbed the biggest ladle. Swoosh! Scoop and pour. Again and again! Fern helped with the biggest ladle too. Faster and faster! Soon, the big pot bubbled, full of soup!

Aunt Rosa beamed. "You figured out the bigger ladle holds more! That made filling the pot so fast!"

Leo zipped. "We filled them up super-fast!" Fern nodded. "The biggest ladle got the most soup with just a few quick scoops!"

"Different bowls hold different amounts," Aunt Rosa smiled. "You are brilliant puzzle-solvers!"

Leo scooped a big spoonful. "Best soup day ever!" he declared.

"Today," Fern chirped, "is going to be AMAZING!" And with happy grins, they raced off to share the yummy soup.
characters: Leo the marble racer, Fern the fawn, Aunt Rosa
